etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English anodine, from Medieval Latin anōdynos (“stilling or relieving pain”), from Ancient Greek ἀνώδυνος (anṓdunos, “free from pain”), from ἀν- (an-, “without”) + ὀδύνη (odúnē, “pain”).
Adjective sense “noncontentious” probably through French anodin (“harmless, trivial”), of same origin.
senses: (pharmacology) Capable of soothing or eliminating pain. [from 16th c.]
(pharmacology) Any medicine or other agent that relieves pain.
(figuratively) A source of relaxation or comfort.
